doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Prof. Davis, and the 'Summertime' chart priced too high for James Brown
summary: Griffin credits Prof. Davis, then recalls offering James Brown an arrangement at union scale and losing the sale.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’ll tell you something too that a lot of people don’t know and wouldn’t know unless I told them, you know Hank Crawford, Hank Crawford had a style of making an eight piece group sound like a big band. He got that, he learned that from my teacher whose name is Mr. William W. Davis. We called him Prof. Davis. He came to Jackson State and he started with Prof. and Hank Crawford and I used to talk about that. Prof Davis was probably one of the best arrangers that I knew. He wrote for the marching band. And we had this arrangement on “I’ll Be Seeing You” you know. And he had a very nice [scats]. Big band [scats]. [Sings] And I’ll be seeing you [scats]. So we’d be marching off the bandstand. But I wrote an arrangement on “Summertime” for the marching band way back in ‘ 63.[scats] So you know I gave it to Pee Wee. And we would open it with James Brown playing it for a whole week. Every time he came through the Apollo Theater, James loved jazz and he would open up with that arrangement. So we’d do [scats] and James would come out doing his thing [scats]. So we did it for the whole week and then at the end of the week, all right, James sent somebody down and said, “James wants to buy the arrangement, man. How much you want for it?” And I told him, “Union scale.” And he said, the guy came down and said that was too much. I wanted James to have the arrangement. I would have given it to him. See I didn’t know that was a big mistake. He said that was too much and that was the last I heard of it you know. And it would have been an honor for him because he just loved it and he would have been playing it all throughout his tour and everything. But I charged him too much and he said that was too much so, and the next thing they’re on the bus and they’re gone. But it was funny. I learned my lesson then.

Maybe, maybe one other time I might have done that and overpriced myself out of a gig. But I found out the best way is to say, “Okay how much are you willing to give me for it.” And then be like that.
